An expansion whose total is greater than the codes it contains is a page of the expansion (valueset-definitions.html#ValueSet.expansion.total, .offset): a code it does not list may be on another page, so its membership is not known and it is accepted unchecked. HL7 6.10.2 takes the page for the whole expansion and reports the code not in the value set.

A ValueSet that excludes a whole code system has none of its codes (valueset-definitions.html#ValueSet.compose.exclude: "Exclude one or more codes from the value set"), directly or through an excluded ValueSet that includes all of it; gofhir applies the exclusion without the CodeSystem, which is not held. HL7 6.10.2 does not decide membership in a system it does not hold and reports nothing.

HL7 6.10.2 does not decide membership in a system it does not hold and reports nothing.

A ValueSet's composition defines it (valueset.html: the expansion is the set of codes the composition gives when expanded); gofhir decides membership by the composition, which does not include the code, and does not read the expansion the ValueSet carries, made against code system versions that may not be the ones held. HL7 6.10.2 decides by the expansion, which lists the code.

A ValueSet whose includes list their concepts has those codes only (valueset-definitions.html#ValueSet.compose.include.concept): US Core's omb-race-category lists five CDC race codes (through VSAC 2.16.840.1.114222.4.11.836) and two NullFlavor codes, so 'bogus' is not a member, whether the CDC race CodeSystem includes its codes or not. HL7 6.10.2 does not decide membership against a CodeSystem that includes none of its codes (content not-present) and reports only that.

A modifier extension changes the meaning of the element that carries it, and one not known means the element cannot be processed as if it were not there (extensibility.html#modifierExtension): an exclusion listing a concept with a modifier extension does not tell whether the code is excluded, so its membership is not known and it is accepted unchecked. HL7 6.10.2 ignores the modifier extension and applies the exclusion.

A profile may name itself in a holder element's type.profile (a Bundle whose entries are Bundles of the profile): its snapshot is the base's with its differential, and the instance bounds the recursion, so the held Bundle is checked against it as against any holder profile (ElementDefinition.type.profile). HL7 6.10.2 generates no snapshot for it ('has no snapshot') and checks nothing against it.

A holder element's type.profile naming a version (hd-obsc|0.1.0) names that definition: the held resource must conform to it (ElementDefinition.type.profile), whatever other version of the same url its own meta.profile names, as each meta.profile is checked too. HL7 6.10.2 skips the holder's profile when meta.profile names its url, in any version or none.

Parameters.parameter.part is defined by a contentReference to Parameters.parameter, whose content rules apply to the current element (ElementDefinition.contentReference): the profile's parameter.resource type.profile applies to part.resource. HL7 6.10.2 does not apply it.

A profile a holder element's type.profile names whose snapshot cannot be generated (its base is not found) cannot be checked against, which is an error for the resource it holds, where it applies; the holder's own profile only names it (ElementDefinition.type.profile), its snapshot not depending on it. HL7 6.10.2 reports the holder's profile as having no snapshot, at the root, and checks nothing against it.

A held resource that conforms to none of its holder's alternatives (ElementDefinition.type.profile) is checked against each of its type, whatever the others' types, so the reasons are errors at the elements they are about, as for alternatives all of its type (where HL7 reports them too). HL7 6.10.2 gives them only as information beside its error when one alternative is of another type (DomainResource).

ElementDefinition.type.targetProfile: the target "must conform to at least one" of the profiles, so a literal reference to a type none of them constrains is an error, whether or not the target resolves. HL7 6.10.4 checks the type only of a target it resolves.
